THE STHIRA PHILOSOPHY

A steady practice for unsteady lives

We built this course around the realization that long, complex 60-minute classes fail busy people. Twenty minutes, done with breath awareness, changes how you carry yourself through the rest of the day.

Bhujangasana - Cobra Pose Demonstrated by Pal Babariya

Most yoga advice tells you to push deeper, bend further, or wake up at 5:00 AM. Sthira asks something much simpler: can you give yourself twenty quiet minutes before the noise of the day starts?

Every session is designed for an ordinary living room floor. No mirrors to judge yourself in, no impossible pretzel shapes, and no guilt when you miss a morning. You just roll your mat back out and begin again.

  • 01

    Grounding over performance

    We do not care whether your heels touch the floor in down-dog or how high your leg lifts. We care whether your breath remains steady and soft while you hold the shape.

  • 02

    Consistency beats duration

    Twenty minutes five days a week reshapes joint mobility and nervous system regulation far more effectively than a grueling ninety-minute class once a month.

  • 03

    Real bodies, real homes

    Filmed with real practitioners in ordinary clothing on a simple mat. If your hamstrings are tight from sitting at a desk all week, this practice was engineered specifically for you.

THE DAILY RHYTHM

Inside a 20-minute daily mat session

A balanced structure designed to wake up the spine, release desk tension, and ground the nervous system before your daily calendar takes over.

00:00 - 04:00 (4 min)

1. Arrive & Ground

Simple diaphragmatic breath work and tall Mountain Posture (Tadasana) to settle the mind and find spinal alignment.

04:00 - 11:00 (7 min)

2. Standing Strength

Active balance postures like Tree Pose (Vrikshasana) and full-body reaches to wake up stabilizing ankle, calf, and hip muscles.

11:00 - 16:00 (5 min)

3. Back & Spine Openers

Prone Cobra Pose (Bhujangasana) and kneeling Camel (Ustrasana) to reverse the forward slump of desk work and open the rib cage.

16:00 - 20:00 (4 min)

4. Seated Twist & Rest

Gentle Vakrasana spinal twists followed by quiet integration so you leave your mat centered and calm.

THE 4-WEEK FOUNDATION CURRICULUM

The Foundation Sequence: All 6 Core Poses

Every posture from our foundation photoshoot, properly framed with zero cropped heads or feet. Click any card to view detailed alignment cues and breathing instructions.

Showing all 6 poses 3 student practitioners
Week 2 Balance Namay Singh
Inspect Alignment Cues ->
Vrikshasana Tree Pose
One-Leg Standing Balance

Root through the four corners of the standing foot. Hands meet overhead in prayer. Develops calm concentration, opens hips, and strengthens ankle stabilizers.

Standing Balance Hip Opening
Cue: Fix gaze on an unmoving spot at eye level to hold stillness.
Week 3 Chest Namay Singh
Inspect Alignment Cues ->
Ustrasana Camel Pose
Kneeling Heart & Spine Opener

From a kneeling stance, lift the sternum upward while hands reach back to clasp the heels. Counters rounded desk posture, opens lungs, and releases hip flexor tightness.

Kneeling Backbend Thoracic Stretch
Cue: Keep thighs pressing forward perpendicular to the mat.
Week 1 Grounding Bobby Kushwah
Inspect Alignment Cues ->
Urdhva Hastasana Mountain Reach
Spine Decompression & Axial Extension

Feet parallel and rooted, fingers interlaced overhead with palms reaching toward the ceiling. Lengthens the entire axial skeleton and creates space between lumbar discs.

Standing Full Stretch Spine Relief
Cue: Draw shoulder blades down the back while reaching wrists high.
Week 4 Cool Down Bobby Kushwah
Inspect Alignment Cues ->
Vakrasana Seated Twist
Thoracic Mobility & Spinal Rotation

Seated on the mat, one leg bent and crossing the other, opposite arm gently hugging the knee. Gently wrings out tension along the spine and relieves lower back tightness.

Seated Rotational Restorative
Cue: Inhale to grow tall through the crown; exhale to rotate from the navel.
Week 2 Spinal Health Pal Babariya
Inspect Alignment Cues ->
Bhujangasana Cobra Pose
Prone Spine & Chest Extension

Lying prone, palms under shoulders, lightly arching the upper back to elevate the collarbones and sternum. Strengthens the spinal erectors without stressing the low back.

Prone Backbend Core Support
Cue: Tuck elbows close to ribs; use back muscles to lift the chest.
Week 3 Elevation Pal Babariya
Inspect Alignment Cues ->
Tadasana on Toes Palm Tree Balance
Elevated Vertical Balance on Balls of Feet

Standing upright on the balls of the feet with hands clasped high overhead. Stretches the abdomen, tests symmetrical equilibrium, and tones calves and foot arches.

Standing Elevation Focus
Cue: Hug inner ankles toward each other to prevent rolling outward.
